data.name: Shrikar
data.gender_notes: Shrikar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who possesses or guards wealth. Derived from Shri (goddess of wealth) and Kar (doer). The name Shrikar carries the meaning “God of Wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Shrikar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Shrikar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Wealth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shrikar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Shrikar" holds great significance in Hindu culture, as it is associated with Shri, the Hindu goddess of wealth and prosperity. This name is believed to bring good fortune, financial stability, and an abundance of riches. It is also a name of respect, as "Shri" is a title used for gods, spiritual gurus, and highly revered individuals.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper spiritual level, the name "Shrikar" signifies being a guardian or protector of one's spiritual wealth – knowledge, wisdom, inner peace, and the connection to the Divine. The inherent meaning of the name serves as a constant reminder for an individual to cherish and protect their spiritual riches, ensuring they are living a meaningful and purposeful life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shrikar symbolizes the one who shrinks away from the transient pleasures of life and seeks the eternal bliss of the divine name "Rama". It is a reverence to Lord Vishnu as the protector and remover of all sorrows.

vedic_reference.note: This name is derived from the Sanskrit word शृङ् (shring), which refers to the God of Wealth, and कर (kar), which means 'to carry'. It is a name used to honor the deity of wealth and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Shrikar, also known as Shrikrishna or Shri Krishna, was an incarnation of the Hindu god Vishnu. He appeared in the Sindhu region around 3200 BCE and played a significant role in the Mahabharata war as an ally to the Pandava princes.

Shrikar, also known as Shri Shankaracharya, was a philosopher and reformer who is considered a founding figure in the Shankhya and Advaita philosophical traditions in Hinduism. He lived around 788 to 820 CE and founded the Dwaita monastic order.
